case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses Bluetooth SIG qualification of products using pre-qualified Bluetooth modules and Windows host stacks. The customer initially planned to qualify an Intel AX210 module with Windows 10 through a simplified Declaration-based registration approach that relied on existing qualified components. After the Bluetooth SIG transition to Qualification Workspace in July 2024, the previously expected Windows 10 qualification path became unavailable because the available Windows 10 Host Subsystem qualifications contained an obsolete HID 1.1 profile. The customer ultimately changed direction and proceeded with a Windows 11-based qualification path. The final registration process involved DID acquisition, registration support, compliance folder preparation, and collection of product documentation.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The main qualification discussion focused on reuse of existing Bluetooth qualifications for a controller module combined with a qualified Windows host stack. The consultant initially confirmed that the controller module and Windows host combination could be qualified without additional Bluetooth testing through Declaration registration. After Qualification Workspace was introduced, available Windows 10 Host Subsystem qualifications were reviewed and found unsuitable for new registrations because they included the deprecated HID 1.1 profile. Qualification Workspace did not allow removal of the obsolete profile through layer selection, preventing reuse of the Windows 10 qualification path. Windows 11 qualifications remained usable, allowing the customer to proceed with qualification using Windows 11 instead.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The decisive factor was qualification asset eligibility under Qualification Workspace rather than whether the controller module itself remained qualified. Existing Windows 10 Host Subsystem qualifications contained deprecated HID 1.1 profile content that prevented their use in new registrations. Because the unwanted profile could not be removed during qualification composition, the Windows 10 path became unavailable for new declarations. Windows 11 qualifications did not have this limitation and therefore provided a valid qualification path.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming that previously qualified component combinations remain reusable after qualification system or policy changes can lead to selecting an invalid qualification path. A project could spend time preparing a Windows 10-based declaration only to discover that the referenced Host Subsystem qualification cannot be used for a new registration. Failure to verify qualification reuse eligibility in Qualification Workspace could cause qualification delays, rework, revised quotations, and a late change in qualification architecture.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a Bluetooth qualification strategy depends on reusing existing Host Subsystem, Controller, or component qualifications, always validate the exact qualification combination in the current Bluetooth SIG qualification system before committing to the qualification plan. Historical qualification status alone is not sufficient because deprecated profiles, policy changes, or Qualification Workspace eligibility rules can invalidate previously viable reuse paths.
